newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary BUX index hits record high at 4,562.83 pts.
newsitem.headline: Hungary BUX index hits record high at 4,562.83 pts.

text.p: The Budapest Stock Exchange's BUX index soared to the 13th successive daily record high on strong gains of most shares traded on Wednesday, traders said.
The BUX index rose 2.23 percent, or 99.36 points, to close at 4,562.83.
"The madness continued," said Gyorgy Czipo of ING Barings, referring to the fact that Hungarian shares rose in the past one month at a pace which astonished traders.
The BUX has risen by more than 10 percent in the first three sessions of 1997 and almost tripled since January 1, 1996.
Traders said attributed the steady rise to last year's macroeconomic figures and corporate results, which substantially strengthened confidence in the Hungarian market.
They said that the stocks on Wednesday rose on the gains of oil and gas company MOL and retailer Fotex.
MOL finished at 2,475 forints, up 70, while Fotex closed at 148 forints, up 18, extending its gains in the last three days to almost fifty percent.
"Several large investors thought in the same time that it was worth buying Fotex at the current price," MKB Securities' Peter Lencs said. "The share is under-valued."
Traders said a larger downwards correction should come soon, perhaps in a few days.
But falling prices in early trading, followed by steep rebounds indicated that the rising trend had not lost steam yet, Lencs added.
Soaring BUX index futures showed unbroken optimism for the longer term. December BUX futures rose 247.50 points to 5,470, while December 1998 futures closed at 6,090 points, up 330.
